description: Define a canonical representation for failure witnesses so that obstruction cores from different parent families can be compared exactly. The aim is to separate genuine recurrence from superficial isomorphism noise.
mathematical_formalization: For each failure witness W, compute canon(W) such that canon(W)=canon(W') iff W and W' are symmetry-equivalent and induce the same forcing pattern.
implementation_hypothesis: Represent each witness as a colored induced subgraph with attachment labels to the extension vertex, then canonicalize with orbit labels before counting frequency.
experiment_seed: Run canonicalization on all cores found in the first atlas pass and compare compression ratio before and after canon().

closest_prior_art.title: Ramsey Number Counterexample Checking and One Vertex Extension Linearly Bound by s and t

novelty_claim: Canonical obstruction cores would let exact Ramsey computation accumulate proof-grade objects instead of re-discovering equivalent failures.
differentiation: The focus is proof object normalization, not generic graph hashing for convenience.
